rounds.hypothesis: O_NOATIME is parsed but never authorized. The VFS open path (InodeHandle::new) and the F_SETFL path (dyn FileLike::update_status_flags) both accept the flag without checking that the caller owns the inode or holds CAP_FOWNER, so open02's unprivileged tcase 1 (open(O_RDONLY|O_NOATIME) on a root-owned 0644 file by fsuid 65534, which has read access through other-r but is not the owner) succeeds where Linux returns EPERM.
rounds.change: Added Inode::check_owner_or_capable() as a default trait method beside Inode::check_permission(), mirroring Linux's inode_owner_or_capable() — it checks fsuid against the inode's uid and falls back to CAP_FOWNER via lsm_hooks::on_capable against the thread's user namespace. Then called it in two places: (1) InodeHandle::new immediately after the existing check_permission call and inside the !O_PATH guard, guarded by status_flags.contains(O_NOATIME), and (2) update_status_flags in file_handle.rs before the existing O_DIRECT validation, gated on the clear-to-set transition (requested flags contain O_NOATIME && current status flags don't). Both placements match Linux: InodeHandle::new is Asterinas's analogue of the tail of may_open(), and update_status_flags is the analogue of setfl(), with check-ordering preserved (EACCES before EPERM at open, O_NOATIME before O_DIRECT at setfl).
rounds.outcome: green: 2 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped — both tcase 0 (missing file without O_CREAT → ENOENT) and tcase 1 (unprivileged O_NOATIME → EPERM) passed, matching the host LTP baseline exactly.

layer: The VFS permission layer, above every filesystem: InodeHandle::new for the open-time check (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:40-50, inside the !O_PATH guard and after the existing access-mode check), and dyn FileLike::update_status_flags for the F_SETFL-time check (kernel/src/fs/file/file_handle.rs:189-202, before the O_DIRECT validation). This exactly matches diagnose.json's owning_layer, which named InodeHandle::new as Asterinas's structural equivalent of Linux's may_open() tail and noted that F_SETFL is independently gated in setfl(). Placing the rule here keeps ramfs/ext2/exfat/virtiofs/pseudofs consistent without per-filesystem duplication, and the !O_PATH guard delivers the O_PATH exemption for free. The ordering after check_permission preserves EACCES ahead of EPERM, which diagnose's host probe confirmed.
generalizes: This is correct for every open caller and every setfl caller, not just open02: (1) InodeHandle::new is the single choke-point for open/openat, covering every path that checks permissions — open02's tcase 1 exercises open(O_RDONLY|O_NOATIME) on an existing file, and the check applies identically to O_WRONLY/O_RDWR, to directories (tested by probe against a root-owned dir), and to device nodes (tested against /dev/null). The O_CREAT-new-file and O_TMPFILE paths bypass InodeHandle::new via new_unchecked_access, but that bypass is provably harmless: ext2 and ramfs both set a new inode's uid from the creator's fsuid (ext2/fs.rs:402, ramfs/fs.rs:1453-1458), so the caller is by construction the owner and check_owner_or_capable would always succeed — that's dead code, not an omission. (2) update_status_flags is the single public setfl-equivalent method on dyn FileLike, reached only from fcntl.rs handle_setfl, and the clear-to-set transition guard matches Linux exactly (fs/fcntl.c:49-52 checks `(arg & O_NOATIME) && !(filp->f_flags & O_NOATIME)`). The check applies to every file type, including sockets/pipes/eventfds (their pseudo/sockfs inodes are uid root in Asterinas rather than the creator's fsuid as in Linux, so fcntl(F_SETFL, O_NOATIME) by non-root on those would EPERM, a behavioral divergence rooted in sockfs uid assignment, but that's pre-existing and orthogonal). (3) The helper Inode::check_owner_or_capable short-circuits when there is no current task or no posix_thread, matching check_permission's pattern and keeping kernel-internal inode construction during boot safe. The rule is inode-type-agnostic, fsuid-based, and mode-bit-independent, as confirmed by diagnose's direct host probe.
fix_summary: Added a VFS-layer owner-or-CAP_FOWNER check for O_NOATIME at both its assertion sites: open time (InodeHandle::new) and F_SETFL time (dyn FileLike::update_status_flags). The check is factored into a new default trait method Inode::check_owner_or_capable, designed against Asterinas's existing Inode trait and credential/capability infrastructure — it uses fsuid (not euid), consults the thread's user namespace (not a filesystem-specific one, since Asterinas does not track per-fs user namespaces), and follows the same short-circuit pattern as check_permission for task-less boot contexts. The two call sites are positioned to preserve errno ordering (EACCES before EPERM, ENOENT before both) and match Linux's check placement (may_open() tail, setfl() before O_DIRECT). The fix does not refactor the two existing open-coded owner-or-capable idioms (Dentry::check_sticky_bit_permission, Path::check_hardlink_source) because those use UserNamespace::get_init_singleton rather than the thread's user namespace, and changing their behavior is out of scope for this fix.
